title: KV burst recovery sentinel: tokens/sec p95 vs hit-rate vs memory hysteresis evaluation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Run a focused evaluation of KV/prefix cache behavior during abrupt inbound traffic bursts and the subsequent recovery period. The goal is to characterize tokens/sec throughput and p95 latency as hit-rate decays and then rebuild during warmup, and to identify memory hysteresis effects (i.e., memory retention vs eviction timing) that cause prolonged p95 regressions after bursts. This ticket spins up a repeatable sentinel harness that drives synthetic mixed-length chat traffic with variable hot-set churn and measures end-to-end generation p95, backend token throughput, prefix-cache hit-rate, and the cache memory footprint over time.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel harness can drive configurable burst shapes (sudden spike, ramp, sustained) and emit time-series at 1s granularity for tokens/sec and request p95
Hitrate-vs-latency curve is produced for at least three memory budgets (baseline, +25%, +50%) and saved to S3 with metadata
Automated regression check: if p95 deteriorates >20% at 95th percentile compared to baseline within 10 minutes following burst, create alertable finding with run snapshot and artifact links
Dashboard tile and comparison chart added to runtime-performance dashboard (showing hit-rate, p95, tokens/sec, mem-usage)
test_plan: Harness: 'burst-sentinel' binary (Go) that simulates client population: 60% short prompts, 30% medium, 10% long; per-req seq-len distribution parameterizable
Burst shapes: instant spike (5x for 60s), linear ramp (1x->4x over 120s), and compound spike+tail (10s spike then 10m decay)
Memory budgets: run three podsized cache configs [base, base*1.25, base*1.5]; for each run, capture KV occupancy and eviction counts
Run cadence: 6 runs per config (random seed variations) during off-peak window; each run 30m baseline, 10m burst, 40m recovery
Metrics collected: tokens/sec, request p50/p95/p99, prefix KV hit-rate (per-key and aggregated), cache memory RSS, eviction rate, kernel scheduling counters
Regression detector: compute rolling baseline from last 5 stable runs and fail if 95th percentile p95 > baseline*1.20 for two consecutive runs
Artifacts: raw traces (1s resolution), aggregated CSVs, flamegraphs for CPU during peak, heap snapshots for memory footprint
instrumentation: Prometheus metrics: redwood_runtime_tokens_total (rate), redwood_req_latency_seconds{quantile}, redwood_kv_prefix_hitrate, redwood_kv_evictions_total, process_resident_memory_bytes
Tracing: distributed traces with span tags 'kv.prefix.hint' and 'kv.hit' to correlate latency tail with cache events
Logging: structured run-summary logs to GCS with run_id, config, seed, and anomaly flags
Dashboards: new panel in runtime-performance showing aligned timeseries (tokens/sec, p95, hit-rate, memory) with run selection dropdown
Regression hook: GitHub Action to ingest CSV summary and post a PR comment if regression triggers
preliminary_results: Run 2026-03-09T02:14Z (base memory): instant spike -> tokens/sec peaked at 9.8x baseline; p95 rose from 42ms to 820ms during spike; hit-rate dropped from 78% to 21%

Recovery tail: with base memory, hit-rate recovered to 60% after ~17 minutes; p95 remained 2.3x baseline for an additional 12 minutes despite hit-rate recovering — indicates memory-induced eviction churn
Increased memory (+25%): peak p95 limited to 560ms; hit-rate bottomed at 33% and recovered in ~9 minutes — improving memory reduced both depth and duration of p95 tail
Eviction patterns: eviction bursts aligned with large contiguous keyset churn for ~90s post-spike; observed high churn in LRU slab rebalancing when under pressure
CPU scheduling: kernel context-switch counters increased 3x during peak, correlating with increased p95; suggests contention at scheduler level for KV servicing threads
anomalies: Observed a persistent 10-12% elevated p95 after recovery for one host where the cache GC thread failed to re-prioritize hot slabs — reproduced under heavy long-sequence traffic mix
One run produced invalid prefix-hint tags in traces due to a new opt-in header being stripped by the test proxy; this run is excluded from rolling baseline
Garbage collection noise: occasional paused intervals (~50-120ms) in Go runtime when heap growth exceeded threshold; variable across versions
next_steps: Implement slab warmup prioritization patch (ENG-WIP-519203-PR) that throttles eviction during first 5 minutes post-spike; land behind feature flag
Add a microbenchmark for prefix-hint propagation to ensure hints survive proxy layers (follow-up ticket if failing)
Triage GC pauses: try go runtime tuning flags and a follow-up harness that isolates Go heap behavior
Automate nightly sentinel runs and hook to regression-detector; if triggered, auto-open ENG issue with run artifacts
